Bill.BriefDescription: Conducting a pilot project to provide the fish and wildlife commission with independent biological information.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing the fish and wildlife commission withindependent biological information; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The fish and wildlife commission shallconduct a pilot project designed to provide biological informationdirectly to the commission from a source independent from thedepartment of fish and wildlife. (2) In implementing the pilot project required by this section, thefish and wildlife commission shall contract with private, independentwildlife biologists to prepare an assessment of current elk and deerresource management and recommend future management plans for elk anddeer. The commission shall execute separate contracts for each of thedepartment of fish and wildlife's administrative units, and requireassessments and plans for each of the game management units establishedwithin the various administrative units. (3) The department of fish and wildlife shall, in a timely matter,grant access to any area or provide any information requested by thewildlife biologists that contract with the fish and wildlife commission p. 1 HB 1250under this section. However, the director of the department of fishand wildlife and other department employees shall have no additionalcontact with the biologists. (4) The results of the assessments and plans developed under thissection by the contract wildlife biologists shall be reported directlyto the fish and wildlife commission by October 31, 2008. (5) Upon the completion of the pilot project, the chair of the fishand wildlife commission shall present a report to the appropriatecommittees of the legislature on the differences between the managementrecommendations made by the independent biologists as compared torecommendations made by employees of the department of fish andwildlife.
